newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down on overseas sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down on overseas sales.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold prices slid rapidly in afternoon trade on Tuesday to end well below New York's Monday close after brisk selling emerged when Europe entered the market, bullion dealers said.
"After a very quiet morning, European professionals were selling," said one gold dealer.
Bullion ended at US$378.40/378.90 an ounce on Tuesday against New York's US$378.80/379.30 close on Monday.
Bearish sentiment ran through the market and some players were said selling the market to force it lower.
Some traders reported producer selling at these levels.
There was little shortcovering and physical demand slowed the price drop only marginally, dealers said.
Morning trade saw some bargain-hunting from local physical buyers, but volumes were thin, bullion traders said.
Gold was supported at $379 per ounce, and little upside potential was seen, they said.
Tael gold was trading about 10 U.S. cents above the loco London price, providing arbitrage opportunities for physical players, dealers said.
"We sold taels in the morning and covered spot gold in the afternoon, making a profit," said one bullion dealer.
Local gold ended HK$14 lower at HK$3,489 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -5.00 from its previous fix at -6.00.
